w1031-01-cold-heart: Lift him too roughly, and this hypothermia rescue could stop his heart. He's been in that freezing lake way too long, and a heart this cold gets twitchy. One hard jolt can tip it into ventricular fibrillation. That's when the heart just quivers instead of pumping. And the scary thing is, the people moving him are only trying to help. So they keep him flat and slide him slowly across the ice, handling him like he's made of glass. And because they're that careful, his heart keeps its slow, steady beat.
w1031-02-phineas-gage: Phineas Gage was tamping blasting powder into a rock in eighteen forty eight, when a spark set it off, and this iron rod shot through his skull. It went in under his left cheekbone, came out the top of his head, and landed about eighty feet away. Somehow he lived, and he was talking within minutes. But the rod had torn through his left frontal lobe, the part of your brain that plans ahead and keeps you in check. And afterward, his friends said he was no longer Gage. All of it started with one spark.
w1031-03-mirror-mint: Spearmint and caraway get their smell from two mirror image molecules, and both are carvone. They have the same atoms and the same bonds, but one is flipped, the way your left hand mirrors your right. And no matter how you turn them, you can't stack one on the other. Chemists call molecules like that kyral. Your nose can tell them apart, because the receptors inside it are kyral too, so each version fits them differently. So if you flip a molecule in a mirror, mint turns into rye bread. Free practice for this on levlprep dot com.
